title: Tiered KV cache ROI workbook (May 2024)
content:
Purpose:
This workbook is an actionable, scenario-driven spreadsheet-style analysis of how a tiered prefix + KV cache (L1 prefix cache that reduces generation length, plus L2 full-KV hits) affects monthly token spend and payback given different hit-rate outcomes. Target audience: product/optimize, serving-runtime, and solutions engineers evaluating a rollout for mid-sized customer workloads.

Top-line summary (one line):
With reasonable engineering investment (~4 engineer-weeks), moving from a low baseline (5% effective cache) to a mid+ scenario (28% effective) reduces monthly inference token costs by ~28% (~$38.7k/mo for the modeled workload), returning investment in ~1.5 months.

Assumptions (conservative/practical):
- Workload: 120,000 requests/day (representative medium SaaS workload).
- Avg tokens per request: 320 (input + generated tokens).
- Cost per token (compute + infra amortized): $0.00012/token (internal blended rate for target clusters).
- Billing window: 30 days/month.
- Baseline behavior: small existing prefix cache and sporadic KV hits (see scenarios).
- Prefix hit token-savings model: a prefix hit short-circuits the majority of the prefix work and often reduces generated tokens by ~60% on average (variable by prompt).
- KV full hit model: a KV hit returns complete cached output and counts as 100% token saving for that request.
- Effective token saving per request = prefix_hit_rate * 0.6 + kv_full_hit_rate * 1.0 (capped at 1.0).

Derived constants used across table: 
- requests/day = 120,000
- tokens/request = 320
- tokens/month = requests/day * tokens/request * 30 = 1,152,000,000 tokens
- baseline_monthly_cost = tokens/month * cost_per_token = 1,152,000,000 * 0.00012 = $138,240

Scenario table (CSV-style):

Notes on the table: tokens and dollar values rounded to two decimals where appropriate. PaybackMonths = engineer_cost / CostSavedPerMonth (engineer_cost assumed $60,000 one-time for implementation + rollout automation). For 'Baseline' the payback is long because savings are small.

Quick derivation (example - Mid scenario):
- Effective token saving fraction = 0.3 * 0.6 + 0.1 * 1.0 = 0.18 + 0.1 = 0.28 (28%)
- Tokens saved / month = 1,152,000,000 * 0.28 = 322,560,000 tokens
- Cost saved / month = 322,560,000 * $0.00012 = $38,707.20
- New monthly cost = $138,240 - $38,707.20 = $99,532.80

Operational impacts and non-token benefits: 
- Latency: prefix hits typically reduce tail generation time (fewer decode steps) — expect median latency drop of 15-40% depending on request distribution. KV full hits return near-instant responses (gateway + cache lookup) offering the largest latency wins for UX-sensitive flows.
- Throughput: reduced GPU decode load allows higher effective throughput per node; can reduce required concurrent machines for same QPS.
- Cold-starts & cache warming: first-of-kind prompts will miss; warm-up policies (pre-warming top-N prefixes per model) dramatically improve early traffic tail performance.
- Memory/storage: larger prefix index and KV store increases memory/disk footprint. For our mid scenario estimate ~200–500GB extra index storage depending on compression and retention TTLs.

Sensitivity: which levers matter most?
- Prefix cache effectiveness scales with prompt repetition and canonicalization (prompt normalization can convert many near-misses into hits). Engineering focus areas: normalization heuristics, stable prompt templates, and trimming non-deterministic metadata.
- KV full hits scale with business logic canonicalization: surfacing deterministic mapping from request -> response (e.g., lookup tables, deterministic completions).
- TTL choice trades off freshness vs hit-rate; doubling TTL from 1h -> 2h often yields 10–25% relative hit-rate lift for stable prompts.

Recommended rollout plan (practical, staged):
1) Measurement baseline (2 weeks): instrument request hashing + prompt fingerprinting to measure natural prefix duplication distribution. Deliverable: sample of top-50 prefix families with frequency and median generated tokens.
2) Quick wins (2–4 weeks): implement prompt normalization for top-5 families + implement L1 prefix cache with 1h TTL + instrumentation. Metric target: move Conservative scenario (~14% effective) with minimal infra.
3) Mid rollout (4–8 weeks): expand normalization rules, increase prefix index to top-500 families, add L2 KV store for deterministic completions, and start pre-warming logic. Target: Mid scenario (28%).
4) Hardening and automation (2–4 weeks): autosyncing index, eviction policies, monitoring/alerts, rollout safe-fallbacks, and canary rules.

Engineering cost estimate (back-of-envelope):
- Stage 1 (measurement): 0.5 engineer-week
- Stage 2 (quick wins): 2 engineer-weeks (1 backend + 1 serving-runtime)
- Stage 3 (mid rollout): 4 engineer-weeks distributed (serving, infra, product)
- Stage 4 (hardening): 2 engineer-weeks
Total: ~8.5 engineer-weeks (approx $60k one-time cost used in payback calc above; adjust for org rates).

Failure modes & risks: 
- Over-aggressive canonicalization can introduce correctness regressions (QA needed on prompt equivalence).
- Latency trade-offs if cache lookups add synchronous RPCs in the hot path (prefer local index + async remote fetch when possible).
- Storage costs may offset token cost savings for extremely high TTLs — model and measure storage delta.

Open questions for reviewers (action items):
- Validation: can ENG provide a 14-day production sample of prefix fingerprint distribution (top N counts + token lengths)? (Assigned: Maya)
- Model-fitting: does serving-runtime have a safe simulation harness to replay requests with proposed prefix normalization? (Assigned: Liam)
- Customer impact: which paying customers would benefit most from an early pilot? (Assigned: Rosa)

Next steps (week-by-week plan):
- Week 1: Collect sample + build baseline metrics (freq, tokens, candidate prefix rules)
- Week 2–3: Implement prefix normalization for top-5, deploy L1 cache behind a feature flag, track hit-rate and cost impact
- Week 4–6: Expand index, enable KV store for deterministic responses, add TTL experimentation flags
- Month 2: Evaluate payback, prepare pilot offering for Dedicated/Private customers who want cost optimization
